title: Complete Hayes translation spectral involution
statement: For every ell>=1 and n>=1, translation F(x)->F(x+1) acts on the binary principal-unit class u by sigma(u)=(1+t)^n u(t/(1+t)) modulo t^(ell+1). Writing tau(u)=u(t/(1+t)), both tau and sigma are involutions, tau is a group automorphism, and the degree-n Mangoldt and squared-discrepancy spectra satisfy A(chi)=chi((1+t)^n)A(chi composed with tau). The tau-fixed dual has exactly 2^ceil(ell/2) characters. Among them, exactly half are forced to vanish when n is odd and none are forced by this mechanism when n is even.

evidence.supports: The class formula, group automorphism, two involutions, commutator quotient, odd-even vanishing dichotomy, and exact Mangoldt-population permutation.
evidence.notes: The universal step is the reciprocal substitution and finite-abelian duality proof. Exhaustive endpoint rows through level eight are mutation controls, not quantifier evidence.

provenance.source: exact reciprocal translation on the truncated binary principal-unit group

notes: This generalizes the translation-forced identity-path split. The forced odd vanishing fraction shrinks with conductor and the even endpoint gets none, so the theorem supplies no standalone REL or Lemire proof credit.
